 Judgment

This reference filed by the petitioner - SLAO under Sections 30 and 31 of KIADB Act, 1966 read with Section 151 of CPC, seeking permission to deposit the compensation amount for the acquired land and for adjudication on the rightful recipient of the award amount deposited by the petitioner.

The case made out by the petitioner in nutshell is that the petitioner for the purpose of development by the KIADB issued a Preliminary Notification under Section 28(1)
bearing No. CI/108/ SPQ/2015 dated 21/22.09.2015 in respect of acquired property and other properties and Final Notification has been issued under Section 28(4) of KIAD Act bearing No.
CI/108/SPQ/2015 dated 22.02.2018. It is further claimed by the petitioner that the respondent filed W.P.No. 24533- 24534/2017, 25334/2017 C.W.. No.24535- 24536/2017, 25877-25880/2017 and the said Writ Petitions came to be disposed off in terms of the order dated 21.11.2017.

Wherein, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka was pleased to direct the SLAO, KIADB to refer the dispute under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act to reference Court, the applicant passed an order L.A.C. No. 128/2022 bearing No. KIADB/METRO/AWARD/426/2018-19 dated 11.09.2018 to deposit the compensation amount before this Court referring the matter to decide the issue in question.
Accordingly, the petitioner filed this reference before this Court for respective prayers stated therein.

.3. The claimant has filed claim statement, wherein, it is admitted about issuance of Preliminary Notification and Final Notification for acquisition of acquired land and claimed that the fair market value of the sites sold in the schedule property is around Rs.8,100/- per Sq. feet and accordingly,
they have negotiated for paying the market value of the sites at the rate of Rs.16,000/- and they are entitled for compensation under the new LA Act, 2013.

The officials of the Government who were involved in the process of land acquisition and payment of the L.A.C. No. 128/2022 compensation,
delayed the process of payment of compensation.

Hence, a suo-moto proceedings is initiated by the Assistant Commissioner, Bengaluru South Sub Division, Bengaluru and passed the impugned order dated 26.05.2017 without issuing the notices to the interested persons.
Hence, the said order has been challenged in W.P.No. 25877/2017 and connected matters.

Accordingly, the impugned order dated 26.05.2017 passed by the Assistant Commissioner in case No. LND/RA(S)18/2016-17 was quashed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka as per final order dated 07.02.2022.

As per the The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State Of Karnataka, Revenue ... on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859198/
2 order of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No. 25877/2017 and connected matters, the Hon'ble High Court has to decide the person who is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: Claimant also claimed that the property bearing No. 87 was Government land out of which an extent of 2.10 guntas was granted in favour of one Ramaiah during the year 1927 and the khatha was also changed to his name in view of the grant.
The said Ramaiah died on 04.07.1938 leaving behind him, his wife and children and they have partitioned the properties as per partition deed dated 29.06.1974 vide registration No. 6328/1974-75.
In the said partition, the property in Sy. No. 87/2 measuring 2.10 acres allotted to the share of Gowramma.

The said Gowramma died intestate leaving behind her, her children namely Rangaswamy, Somashekar,
Ramakrishna and Savithri as surviving legal heirs.

.5. Claimant claimed that meantime the property bearing Sy. No. 87/2 was acquired for L.A.C. No.
128/2022 benefit of BDA under Preliminary Notification under Section 17(1) of the B.D.A. Act dated 23.03.1988 followed by Final Notification under Section 19(1) of the B.D.A. Act dated 19.10.1994.

The said acquisition proceedings and Final Notification have been challenged in W.P.No.
31892/2009 and connected matters.

In the said matters, issue was raised as to whether the Sy. No.
87 was the Government land or not.
In the said writ petition, the B.D.A. claimed that the property in Sy. No. 87 was a Government land.
Meantime, the B.D.A. wanted to ascertain the details of the grants made in Sy. No. 87 and accordingly, the matter has been referred to the Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru.

In view of the said letter from the B.D.A., the Special Deputy Commissioner initiated the proceedings by directing the Special Tahsildar, L.A.C.
No. 128/2022 Bengaluru South Taluka to make an inquiry as to auctions and the grants made in Sy.
No. 87 and to furnish the details.

The Special Tahsildar has initiated the proceedings and after holding an inquiry, filed report dated 05.04.2005 to the Special Deputy Commissioner along with index of land, Mysore Revision settlement Register etc., which shows the allotment of property to various persons.

.6. Claimant claimed that in inquiry proceedings in RRT (North) CR-16/2005-06, Smt. Saraswathi appeared before the Deputy Tahsildar and filed certain documents including Manjuri- Hukum dated 05.07.1929, partition deed dated 29.06.1974 and mutation is also made out in MR No. 114/2004-05 and given a finding that the property originally granted to Ramaiah.
It is further stated that the said property has been conveyed in favour of L.A.C. No. 128/2022 Smt. Revathi N, Rekha N, Damodhara and N. Chandrashekar under a registered sale deed dated 12.11.2009.

Thereafter, the said Smt.
Revathi and others had offered the said property for joint development in favour of the claimant - Developer M/ s. Amalgamated Property Developers as per the terms of the Joint Development Agreement dated 31.01.2011.
.7.
Claimant further claimed that in the Joint Development Agreement, the sites involved in this case along with other sites allotted to the share of claimant.
Subsequently, the B.D.A. has also sanctioned the layout plan vide sanction plan dated 04.03.2014.
The Developer has developed the said property in the name and style of "Classic Orchards Phase-III Layout" and sold sites in favour of subsequent purchasers.
Accordingly, the claimant L.A.C. No. 128/2022 claimed that it has acquired the valid right, title and interest over the site involved in this case along with other sites.

sentences.text: Accordingly, prayed for the relief claimed in this reference.

.8. The respondent No. 2 BMRCL has filed objections stating that the beneficiary of acquisition BMRCL sent a compensation package to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, fixing the market value at Rs. 39,740/- per sq. meters through letter dated 27.07.2018.
It is stated that after receipt of compensation package from BMRCL, Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB issued notice under Section 29(2) to the Khatedars.
During inquiry the SLAO noticed that there existed W.P. No. 24533-24534/2017.

It is stated that W.P. No. 25334-25335/2017 and W.P. No.
25877-25880/2017 L.A.C. No. 128/2022 pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in- respect of the property in question.
In view of the same, the SLAO could not take decision regarding ownership and apportionment of compensation.

Hence, he proceeded to pass General Award and also deposited the compensation package into the Civil Court and referred the matter to the Court under Section 30 and 31 of L.A. Act, for disbursement of compensation after determining the rights of the parties.

It is stated that the respondent No. 2 BMRCL who is beneficiary of acquisition will not be liable to pay interest on the awarded compensation amount as also held in the decision 1995(5)
SCC 577 (SLAO Vs. Puttaiah and others).
.9.
In order to prove claimant's case, its Managing Partner Sri. Rathan Babulal Lath is examined as PW.1.

The documents got marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
L.A.C. No. 128/2022 .10.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimant is entitled to receive the compensation amount in this case?"
.11.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in the affirmative, for the following:
REASONS .12. Point No.1: This reference has been referred to this Court under Section 29 of the KIADB Act, to decide the rightful recipient of the award amount deposited by the petitioner.

In the case on hand, it is undisputed fact that the schedule property has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 22.09.2015 and Final Notification dated 22.02.2018 and General Award passed on 20.08.2022.

It is also admitted fact in this case that the respondent has filed W.P.No.
24533- L.A.C. No. 128/2022 534/2017, W.P.No.25334-25335/17 and W.P.No. 25877- 880/2017, that have been disposed off on 21.11.2017.
Thereafter, Final Notification has been issued and the award has been passed.

Subsequently, as on 19.09.2022 the claimant deposited a sum of Rs.
39,14,943/- out of Rs. 48,93,678/- claiming that they have deducted 20% towards income tax.
.13.
As discussed earlier, the reference is made to the Court and the amount has been deposited to the Court by the petitioner in order to decide the rightful recipient of the award amount.
Hence, the The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State Of Karnataka, Revenue ... on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859198/

sentences.text: 4 Court has to give a specific finding that who is the owner of the acquired land as described in the schedule property.
In the case on hand, the claimant M/s. Amalgamated property Developers claimed that it is the absolute owner of the schedule property.

The claim of the claimant is that the property bearing Sy. No. 87 was Government land, out of which, an extent of 2 acres 10 guntas of land L.A.C. No. 128/2022 was granted in favour of Ramaiah during the year 1927 and accordingly,
the khatha has been changed in his name.

Subsequently after the death of said Ramaiah, his surviving LRs have entered into the partition deed dated 29.06.1974 and in the said partition, the property in Sy. No. 87/2 measuring 2 acres 10 guntas of land allotted to the share of Gowramma.

After the death of Gowramma, her children namely Rangaswamy, Somashekar, Ramakrishna and Savithri succeeded to the said property and thereafter, as per the Preliminary Notification issued by the B.D.A. dated 23.03.1988 followed by Final Notification dated 19.10.1994.
The said property has been acquired by the B.D.A., and the same has been challenged in W.P.No. 31892/2009 and connected cases.
Subsequently, there is dispute regarding extent of grant of the land and inquiry has been held in RRT (North)CR-16/2005-06.

Wherein, it is held that the property originally granted to Ramaiah and L.A.C. No. 128/2022 in the said proceedings, it is also held that the property has been conveyed in favour of Smt. Revathi, N Rekha, N. Damodhara and N. Chandrashekar under a registered sale deed dated 12.11.2009.

Thereafter, the said Revathi and others have offered the said property for joint development in favour of the Developer M/s. Amalgamated Property Developers as per the terms of the Joint Development Agreement dated 31.01.2011.

Subsequently the B.D.A. has sanctioned layout plan vide sanction plan dated 04.03.2014.
.14.
The case made out by the claimant is that it has entered into the Joint Development Agreement with the owner of the property as on 31.01.2011 as per Ex.P.13.
Thereafter, the land owner and claimant entered into an agreement of sharing of sites as per Ex.P.11 as on 08.04.2014.

In this case,
the claimant claims right over 'B' schedule property mentioned in Ex.P.11 and as per the said schedule, 15 sites in total L.A.C. No. 128/2022 measuring 17378 Sq. feet has been allotted to the share of claimant, which is the 32.6% of the total share and remaining 67.4% share has been retained by the land owners who have entered into a joint development agreement with claimant.
Accordingly, the claimant claiming right over the acquired land involved in this case.

.15. In the case on hand, the ownership of Smt. Revathi and others over the property involved in this case is not in dispute and the Competent Revenue Authorities in full pledged inquiry held that they have acquired valid right, title and interest over the property.
The said Smt Revathi and others purchased the property under a registered sale deed dated 12.11.2009 as per Ex.P.5.
As per the said document, surviving LRs of Gowramma jointly sold the property to Smt. Revathi and others.
.16. After the aforesaid sale deed Ex.P.5 the property has been mutated in the name of Smt. Revathi L.A.C. No. 128/2022 and others.

Subsequently said Smt. Revathi and other entered into a Joint Development Agreement with claimant to develop the property and therefore the layout has been formed and again the owner of the property namely Smt. Revathi and others entered into an agreement of sharing of sites with claimant.
The said sharing of sites is also not in dispute.

Further even according to the Gazette notification issued by the Government and produced before the court by the petitioner at Annexure B at ink page No. 21 and Sl. No. 46 disclose that the said property belongs to claimant.
Of course, there is a reference of Government and claimant, but there is no The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State Of Karnataka, Revenue ...

5 material on record to show that the Government has right over the said property, but that has been belongs to claimant.

Therefore, the oral and documentary evidence produced before the Court sufficiently shows that the claimant is the absolute owner of the acquired property and claimant is entitled for the L.A.C. No. 128/2022 compensation.

Accordingly, the above point is answered in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is hereby allowed.

Claimant M/s. Amal Gamatech  Developer is entitled to receive compensation in respect of the land bearing Identification No.R6-DP1/A Plot No. 44 in Sy. No.87 measuring 111.41 Sq. Meters of Kothanur village, Bangaluru South Taluka with statutory benefits.

The claimant shall has to execute an indemnity bond with one surety, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount it is going to receive in this case.
L.A.C. No. 128/2022 Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the SG-I, transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections, pronounced in open Court on this the 10th day of June, 2024.)

(Padma Prasad), II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge,
Bangalore.
